name: Grafana Mimir — Ingest & Storage Architecture (CALM)
description: A CALM 1.1 representation of Grafana Mimir's ingest-to-storage architecture: components that receive and distribute writes (Distributors), buffer and flush time-series (Ingesters), durable chunk/object storage, and background components (Compactor, Store-Gateway) that manage long-term storage and queryability.

nodes.name: Mimir Distributor
nodes.description: Receives write (ingest) requests from Prometheus remote_write or other write clients and shards/forwards them to ingesters. Handles fanout, request buffering, and basic validation.

nodes.name: Mimir Ingester
nodes.description: Buffers incoming series in-memory (or WAL) and periodically flushes encoded chunks to object storage. Responsible for replication, series lifecycle, and handing over data to long-term storage.

nodes.name: Ingester Ring (Consistent-Hashing Ring)
nodes.description: Membership and shard ring used by distributors and ingesters to locate which ingesters own which series. Implements consistent hashing and token assignment for replication.

nodes.name: Object Store / Chunk Storage
nodes.description: Durable object storage used to persist encoded TSDB chunks and index data (e.g., S3, GCS, Azure Blob). Acts as the long-term storage backend for flushed chunks and compactor output.

nodes.name: Compactor
nodes.description: Background component that compacts smaller chunk files into larger, query-efficient objects and removes old/overwritten data according to retention rules. Helps reduce object store costs and speeds up queries over long time ranges.

nodes.name: Store-Gateway
nodes.description: Component that provides read access to long-term objects in object storage on behalf of queriers. It caches index/blocks and stitches series from object store for queries spanning historical data.

relationships.description: Distributor forwards incoming write requests (remote_write) to the appropriate ingesters based on the ring/sharding policy.
Distributor consults the ingester ring to locate owners for series and to drive request fanout/replication decisions.
Ingesters register with and consult the ring for token assignment, replication targets, and membership information.
Ingesters flush encoded TSDB chunks and index data to the configured durable object store for long-term retention.
Compactor reads and writes chunk objects in object storage to perform compaction and retention operations.
Store-Gateway fetches persisted blocks and index data from object storage to serve historical queries and to populate its cache.
Store-Gateway coordinates with the Compactor to understand compacted layout and to assist in retrieval/serving of compacted objects.
